authoringNotes: Original introductory US aide-role exercises, not a state CNA exam bank or a clinical protocol.
Facility-policy scenarios state their assumptions; tasks, delegation and escalation must match local training and policy.
Require qualified nurse-educator review before publishing. No medications, dosage advice or independent diagnosis.
Hard tiers are multi-constraint reasoning within the aide role; Golden/Boss remain off pending curation.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes gloves and hand hygiene in resident care?
choices: Gloves do not replace required hand hygiene
Gloves remove the need to clean hands after care
One pair of gloves is suitable for multiple residents
Hand hygiene is needed only when gloves tear
questions.explanation: Gloves are a barrier, not a replacement for hand hygiene. Clean hands at the appropriate moments, including after removing gloves.
hints: Consider how contamination could move between hands, equipment, residents, or tasks.

questions.prompt: To whom do Standard Precautions apply in healthcare?
choices: All patients regardless of known infection status
Only patients with a confirmed infectious diagnosis
Only patients whose laboratory results are pending
Only patients in rooms with isolation signage
questions.explanation: Standard Precautions apply to all patients. Additional precautions may be required, but absence of a known diagnosis does not remove baseline precautions.
hints: Consider how contamination could move between hands, equipment, residents, or tasks.

questions.prompt: In this facility exercise, which note meets the rule to record observable facts rather than diagnoses?
choices: Resident stated that the room was spinning at 10:15
Resident definitely has an inner-ear disease
Resident is pretending because yesterday was normal
Resident needs a new prescription chosen by the aide
questions.explanation: The exercise rule requires an observation and the resident statement, not an unsupported diagnosis. Report the change to the supervising nurse as directed.
hints: Separate what was observed or reported from an unsupported clinical conclusion.

questions.prompt: In this exercise, the aide procedure requires uncertain tasks to be checked with the supervising nurse. Which concept describes that action?
choices: Escalation
Delegation
Care plan
Objective documentation
questions.explanation: Escalation brings a concern or uncertainty to an authorized supervisor. It does not itself authorize a new task or replace the resident care plan.
hints: Check the task against the aide training, authorization, and supervising nurse instructions.

distractorKnowledge.definition: Assignment of a task within stated authority and limits
distractors: A factual record of an observation and its time
A request for review of an unresolved concern
A resident-specific outline of approved care
distractorKnowledge.explanation: In this exercise, delegation assigns a task with defined boundaries. The aide still follows training, the stated limits and the supervising nurse instructions.
hints: Compare the purpose of this concept with the other functions described.

distractorKnowledge.definition: A resident-specific outline of approved care needs
distractors: A request for an authorized person to review a concern
A factual note of a single observation and its time
An assignment of a task with defined authority limits
distractorKnowledge.explanation: A care plan guides resident-specific care. It is not a substitute for reporting changes or resolving an unclear task with the supervising nurse.
hints: Compare the purpose of this concept with the other functions described.

distractorKnowledge.definition: A factual record of observations without unsupported conclusions
distractors: Assignment of a task with stated authority and limits
A resident-specific outline of approved care needs
A request for supervisory review of an unresolved concern
distractorKnowledge.explanation: Objective documentation separates observed facts from guesses. A record may include the resident own statement and the time of the observation.
hints: Compare the purpose of this concept with the other functions described.

questions.prompt: Which action respects resident privacy during personal care?
choices: Provide appropriate covering and a private care space
Discuss the resident care with unrelated visitors
Keep the door open for spectators during all care
Display the resident information in a public corridor
questions.explanation: Privacy is a resident right. Explain the care and provide appropriate privacy rather than exposing the resident or discussing care publicly.
hints: Consider the resident choice, dignity, and appropriate communication with the care team.

questions.prompt: After completing care for one resident, what should happen before care requiring gloves for another resident?
choices: Remove gloves, clean hands and use a new pair
Keep the same gloves if they look visibly clean
Wash the used gloves and carry them to the next room
Wipe the gloves on a towel and continue working
questions.explanation: Change gloves between patients and perform appropriate hand hygiene. Reusing the same pair can transfer contamination to another resident.
hints: Consider how contamination could move between hands, equipment, residents, or tasks.

questions.prompt: What should guide PPE selection under Standard Precautions?
choices: The anticipated exposure during the care task
Only the resident preferred clothing color
Only whether the room has a television
Only the distance from the nursing station
questions.explanation: PPE selection depends on anticipated exposure. A label or unrelated room attribute does not by itself describe the exposure involved in the task.
hints: Consider how contamination could move between hands, equipment, residents, or tasks.

questions.prompt: A resident makes a care preference known. Which response best supports respectful care?
choices: Listen and communicate the preference to the care team
Dismiss the preference because routines are always identical
Tell unrelated visitors to decide without involving the resident
Hide the preference so it cannot affect the scheduled care
questions.explanation: Resident-centered care respects choices and communicates them to the team. Care planning and safety questions should be resolved with the appropriate staff.
hints: Consider the resident choice, dignity, and appropriate communication with the care team.

questions.prompt: A resident declines a scheduled nonurgent bath. Under the exercise procedure, what should the aide do?
choices: Respect the refusal and notify the nurse for follow-up
Force the bath because it appears on the schedule
Record the bath as completed to avoid a late task
Ask an unrelated visitor to pressure the resident
questions.explanation: The exercise procedure requires respecting refusal and notifying the nurse. Report what occurred; do not coerce the resident or falsely document completed care.
hints: Consider the resident choice, dignity, and appropriate communication with the care team.

questions.prompt: The exercise care plan requires two trained staff for a transfer, but only one is available. What should the aide do?
choices: Obtain the required assistance before the transfer
Transfer alone to keep the schedule unchanged
Ask an untrained visitor to take the second role
Ignore the plan because the resident feels ready
questions.explanation: Follow the stated plan and seek trained help. Scheduling pressure does not change the exercise requirement or authorize an unsupported transfer.
hints: Use the stated care plan and required verification before proceeding.

questions.prompt: During routine care, a resident reports new discomfort. The exercise procedure requires prompt reporting of new symptoms. What is the aide next step?
choices: Notify the nurse and report the resident words and observations
Diagnose the cause and select a new medication
Wait until the next day because discomfort is subjective
Change the care plan independently without consulting anyone
questions.explanation: The stated procedure assigns assessment decisions to the nurse. The aide contributes timely observations and the resident report rather than an independent diagnosis.
hints: Separate what was observed or reported from an unsupported clinical conclusion.

questions.prompt: After a soiled-care task, an aide must assist with a clean-care task for the same resident. What is the best transition?
choices: Remove gloves, clean hands and prepare fresh task-appropriate PPE
Keep soiled gloves because it is the same resident
Handle clean supplies first and clean hands afterward
Wipe soiled gloves and use them for every remaining task
questions.explanation: A dirty-to-clean transition must avoid carrying contamination into clean care. Change gloves and perform hand hygiene before continuing the appropriate task.
hints: Consider how contamination could move between hands, equipment, residents, or tasks.
questions.evidence: Current gloves contacted soiled material; the next task uses clean supplies.
constraints: Use PPE appropriate to the next exposure

questions.prompt: A care entry was marked complete, but the resident declined the task. What should the aide do under the stated record-correction policy?
choices: Report the discrepancy and correct the record through the approved process
Leave the entry because the task was originally scheduled
Erase all earlier entries to prevent questions about the record
Complete the task against the resident wishes to match the entry
questions.explanation: A correction should preserve an accurate, accountable record. The stated process addresses the error without coercion or hiding the original entry.
hints: Distinguish scheduled care from completed care and preserve an accurate correction history.
questions.evidence: The entry says complete; the aide observed and reported a refusal.
constraints: Do not erase the audit history

questions.prompt: A supervisor asks an aide to perform an unfamiliar task. Under this exercise policy, only trained and authorized tasks may be assigned. What is the best response?
choices: Explain the training gap and seek a trained authorized staff member
Attempt the task quietly using instructions from a visitor
Agree to do it and report the gap only if a problem occurs
Change the authorization record to show uncompleted training
questions.explanation: The policy requires both training and authorization. Raising the gap protects the resident while allowing the supervisor to arrange appropriate care.
hints: Check the task against the aide training, authorization, and supervising nurse instructions.
questions.evidence: The aide has neither training nor authorization for this specific task.

questions.prompt: One resident reports an urgent concern while another waits for routine grooming. The exercise policy requires urgent concerns to be escalated immediately. What plan best fits both needs?
choices: Notify the nurse about the concern and arrange coverage for routine care
Finish all grooming before telling anyone about the concern
Leave both residents without telling the team where help is needed
Diagnose the concern alone and cancel all other care for the shift
questions.explanation: The supplied priority rule requires escalation. Communicating and coordinating coverage addresses competing care needs without taking over licensed assessment decisions.
hints: Apply the stated urgency rule while coordinating coverage for other care needs.
questions.evidence: The concern meets the exercise urgent-reporting criterion; grooming is nonurgent.

questions.prompt: A verbal request conflicts with a documented two-person assistance plan. The nurse can be reached and no emergency is described. What is the safest next step under the exercise policy?
choices: Pause the transfer and clarify the conflict with the nurse
Follow the faster request and document the conflict tomorrow
Choose the instruction that requires less staffing effort
Ask a visitor to decide which instruction should be ignored
questions.explanation: Clarification resolves the conflict before action. Neither convenience nor an untrained third party establishes authorization to change the resident plan.
hints: Resolve conflicting instructions through the authorized care team before acting.
questions.evidence: The written plan requires two staff; the new request would use one.
constraints: Use the documented plan until clarified

questions.prompt: In this exercise, the facility requires suspected mistreatment to be reported immediately through its safeguarding route. What should the aide do after witnessing concerning behavior?
choices: Follow the reporting route and give factual observations
Wait for other residents to investigate the behavior
Promise to keep the concern secret from the care team
Post the resident details publicly to request opinions
questions.explanation: The exercise reporting rule directs timely safeguarding escalation. Factual observations support review without delaying protection or exposing resident details publicly.
hints: Follow the stated reporting route using factual observations and appropriate privacy.

questions.prompt: This facility requires two approved resident identifiers before a listed care task. One identifier does not match. What should the aide do?
choices: Pause and resolve the mismatch using the approved procedure
Continue because the resident is in the expected room
Change the label to make it match without checking
Ask another resident to guess who the person is
questions.explanation: The stated identification procedure is not complete. Resolve the mismatch before proceeding rather than relying on room location or a guess.
hints: Use the stated care plan and required verification before proceeding.

questions.prompt: A shared device is labeled awaiting cleaning, but a coworker says it is probably ready. Under the exercise policy, what should the aide do?
choices: Obtain verified clean equipment or complete the approved cleaning process
Use the device because a coworker expressed confidence
Remove the cleaning label without checking its status
Hide the device status so the task can proceed on time
questions.explanation: The label is unresolved evidence under the supplied process. A verified clean device or an approved cleaning completion resolves the status; confidence alone does not.
hints: Consider how contamination could move between hands, equipment, residents, or tasks.
questions.evidence: The device label says cleaning pending; no completion record is available.
constraints: Follow facility and device cleaning instructions

questions.prompt: True or false: gloves eliminate the need for hand hygiene after removing them.
questions.explanation: Hands can become contaminated during care or glove removal. Hand hygiene remains necessary after gloves are removed.
hints: Consider how contamination could move between hands, equipment, residents, or tasks.

questions.prompt: True or false: under a factual-documentation policy, recording a resident exact statement can be appropriate when clearly attributed.
questions.explanation: An attributed statement records what the resident said. It should be distinguished from a diagnosis or an inference the aide has not established.
hints: Distinguish scheduled care from completed care and preserve an accurate correction history.
